Configuration values set outside the code, such as the admin list.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File setup and imports
sections.what: Describes the purpose and brings in the session lookup, the auth settings and the environment reader.
sections.why: The header states the rule that the admin list is checked against the signed-in email.
sections.watch_out: The session lookup needs the same auth settings used at sign-in, or sessions will not be read.

sections.name: isAdminSession
sections.title: Admin check
sections.what: Returns true only when someone is signed in and their email, in lower case, is on the admin list. An empty list means nobody is an admin.
sections.why: The fail-closed default is clear in the code: no list means no admin access.
sections.watch_out: Only the lower-case form is compared, so the admin list must also be stored in lower case, which the settings file does.

summary: Decides whether the signed-in user is an admin, by checking their email against a configured list of admin emails.
purpose: Lets pages restrict admin-only areas to the people named in the admin list.
why: The header states the rule: the signed-in user's email must be in the admin list. The reason for using email rather than a role is not stated in the code.
how: 1) Reads the admin email list from the settings. 2) If the list is empty, refuses everyone. 3) Gets the signed-in session and the user's email in lower case. 4) Returns true only if that email is on the list.
inputs: The admin email list from the environment settings, and the current signed-in session.
outputs: A yes or no answer: true only for a signed-in user whose email is on the list.
risks: Access depends entirely on the email the sign-in provider supplies. An empty admin list locks everyone out, including the owner, which is the safe default but can surprise a new setup.
debug: If an admin cannot get in, check that ADMIN_EMAILS contains their email in lower case with no extra spaces, and that they are signed in. Check the sign-in provider returns an email at all.
